title: Model
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. This ensures that the origin of the coordinate system aligns with the global coordinate system. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin the first loop by drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0062, 0.0). Then, draw the second line from (0.0062, 0.0) to (0.0062, 0.002). Follow this by drawing the third line from (0.0062, 0.002) to (0.0, 0.002), and finally, draw the fourth line from (0.0, 0.002) back to the origin (0.0, 0.0). After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.0062 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Ensure that the sketch remains aligned with the coordinate system by rotating it using Euler angles of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and translating it using a vector of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0. To transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional model, extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction. Do not extrude in the opposite direction. This operation will create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the model are a length of 0.00625, a width of 0.002, and a height of 0.75.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0062, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0062, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0)
    .lineTo(0.0062, 0.0)
    .lineTo(0.0062, 0.002)
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.002)
    .close()
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
